`man`: show a manual page.

## Synopsis

<strong>man</strong> \[<em>section</em>\] <em>name</em>

## Description

<strong>man</strong> finds the manual page for <em>name</em>, formats it for the terminal and shows it through a pager. Pages are man(7) source, as on Linux, kept as <em>/usr/share/man/man</em>section<em>/</em>name<em>.</em>section<em>.</em> With no <em>section</em>, sections 1, 8, 5 and 7 are searched, in that order.

On a terminal, the page is laid out to the terminal's width, with bold and italic text (italics show underlined), and piped to <strong>$MANPAGER</strong> or <strong>$PAGER</strong>, else <strong>less</strong>(1). Into a pipe or a file, the plain text is written, 80 columns wide.

## Environment

<strong>MANPATH</strong>
: The manual trees to search, separated by <strong>:</strong>; <em>/usr/share/man</em> by default.

<strong>MANPAGER PAGER</strong>
: The pager, run with <strong>sh -c</strong>; the first set is used.

<strong>LESS</strong>
: Left as it is; when it isn't set, <strong>man</strong> runs its pager with <strong>LESS=-R</strong> (as man-db does), so <strong>less</strong>(1) shows bold and underline instead of their escape sequences.

## Page format

The formatter understands this part of man(7), and ignores other requests:

<strong>.TH</strong> <em>title section</em>
: The page's title, shown in its header and footer.

<strong>.SH .SS</strong>
: A section heading, a subsection heading.

<strong>.PP .P .LP</strong>
: A new paragraph (so does a blank line).

<strong>.TP</strong>
: A tagged paragraph: the next line is the tag, the lines after it the indented body.

<strong>.IP</strong> <em>tag</em>
: A tagged paragraph with the tag given.

<strong>.RS .RE</strong>
: Indent further, and back.

<strong>.B .I</strong>
: The line in bold, in italics.

<strong>.BR .RB .BI .IB .IR .RI</strong>
: Words in fonts taking turns, with no spaces between them (quote a word to keep spaces in it).

<strong>.nf .fi</strong>
: Lines as they are (no filling), and filled again.

<strong>.br .sp</strong>
: A line break, a blank line.

<strong>.\\"</strong>
: A comment.

In text: <strong>\\fB \\fI \\fR \\fP</strong> change the font (bold, italic, roman, the previous one); <strong>\\-</strong> is a minus, <strong>\\e</strong> and <strong>\\\\</strong> a backslash, <strong>\\(em</strong> a dash, and  nothing.

## Exit status

0 on success; 1 with no name given; 16 if no page was found.

## Examples

```text
man ls
man 1 sh
man less > less.txt
```

## Notes

There are no options and no <strong>-k</strong>; tables, other macros and other escapes are not supported.

## See also

<strong>less</strong>(1)
